markers.reading: At the opening, the party has already traveled in Limbo for more than twelve hours after starting in the morning. This is a retrospective entry-to-opening anchor, not new travel after the opening.

evidence.quote: DM: It's like, what is... It's not like it's decaying in the next eight hours. And you've been with... Between every... I mean, you're hungry at this point. You've probably been traveling in Limbo for o—
DM: ... more than 12 hours. You started in the morning, so... Although actually the food that you made from the tree was incredibly filling.

duration.basis: DM estimates more than twelve hours of preceding Limbo travel

relative.anchor: departure/entry into Limbo before the opening

time.basis: DM says the preceding journey started in the morning; no civil date spoken

markers.reading: The party completes a long rest in Rai’s sanctuary before departing.

Unknown: Yeah. Yeah. Short rested.
DM: No, long rest.

evidence.quote: DM: So m— racing forward, uh, you get a little bit of distance from this thing, like you're maybe 30 minutes ahead of it, ahead of this wave of expanding explosive, explosive chaos—
DM: … as you appear in the monks' area with something like 30 minutes before a chaos bomb hits the monastery.
Delwath: Takes an hour.
DM: Oh, sorry. You have an hour and a half before the—
DM: Yes. It, it doesn't act— the ritual could actually just only take five minutes. The point is you have 30 minutes of spare time. I forgot the ritual. I said the ritual took an hour.
DM: In 30 minutes... Well, in an hour and a half, uh—

offset.basis: corrected forecast of the chaos front’s arrival

time.basis: DM explicitly corrects the deadline to an hour and a half

markers.note: A possible five-minute ritual is floated in the correction, but the retained ninety-minute deadline is repeated; it does not establish another rest or ninety completed minutes here.

DM: Oh, sorry. You have an hour and a half before the—

markers.reading: The party crosses the rainbow bridge into the elven forest in the middle of the night, less than one Material Plane day after entering Limbo.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay. You all run onto the rainbow bridge as the monastery decays around you, moments before the chaos explosion hits, and you race across, the last ones, the monks having all gone before you while you were talking to Rai, run across the bridge and return to the Elven Forest, uh, in the middle of the night, not even a day having passed—
DM: … since you entered Limbo, and all now level 20.

time.basis: DM’s direct return anchor; no numerical clock or date is spoken

duration.basis: DM says not even a day since entry into Limbo; world clock

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: No current-session civil date is independently spoken. The manifest supplies DR 1749-09-16 as both working endpoints; entry is recalled as morning and return is middle of the night less than one world day later.
yamlCheck.explanation: The rest and ritual establish local Limbo elapsed time, whose relation to the world clock is variable. The return can fit late on the YAML date, but the midnight watch can also straddle a civil boundary. Neither zero nor one world-date transition is independently settled.

boundaryUncertainties.reading: Middle of the night spans both sides of civil midnight; the transcript gives no date or clock within that watch.

alternatives.reading: Return late on the same civil day as the morning entry.
Return early on the following civil day, still less than twenty-four world hours after entry.
